text: Once the interface stops pretending the machine is a speaker, other structures have to take its place.
What’s left is an assertion without an asserter.
The persona absorbs the breakdown and turns it into social repair.
Claims nobody committed to, absorbed into the common background and repeated as if someone had meant them — a counterfeit tradition.
The LLM is the first one we made pretend to be a person.
Who is speaking, who is at stake, and who is the author are one question.
near: We can use LLMs to get there

text: Perhaps the next major movement in LLM interface design is about making machines unmistakably machines.
Matched friction of this kind is where authorship happens; removing it removes the author.
